name: Thucydides, son of Melesias
desc: Thucydides, son of Melesias, was a politician of ancient Athens and for a number of years the leader of the powerful conservative faction. Born in the deme of Alopeke to a noble family, he was a relative of Cimon, whom he succeeded as leader of the conservatives, and he opposed Pericles. He is likely related to the later historian Thucydides, son of Olorus, though the details are uncertain. His strength peaked after the First Peloponnesian War, when he had his supporters sit together in the assembly. According to Plutarch, he was ostracized for ten years in 442 BCE after Pericles answered his charge of profligacy.
